name: Mastic (Pistacia lentiscus resin)
short: On the skin, gum mastic in a surgical adhesive caused allergic contact dermatitis (patch-test series). By mouth, two trials of up to 3 months reported it well tolerated.
text: Taken by mouth, Chios mastic was well tolerated in the cited trials: in an 8-week placebo-controlled pilot trial in 179 volunteers with raised cholesterol (156 analysed), no gastrointestinal, liver or renal adverse events were recorded, and in a 3-month placebo-controlled trial in 106 adults with well-controlled high blood pressure, supplementation was well tolerated; the abstracts do not give adverse-event counts. Applied to the skin, gum mastic is an ingredient of a liquid adhesive used after surgery, and in a patch-testing series 13 of 18 patients allergic to that adhesive reacted to gum mastic, often with co-reactions to fragrance materials, while 1 of 250 patients without postoperative dermatitis tested positive. In rats, mastic by gavage showed no genotoxic effects in a bone marrow micronucleus test and no toxicity signs at the dose tested (animal data). No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
